guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
models: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
guitar.notes: Confirmed and refined — Gary Moore's 1959 Les Paul "Greeny" (previously owned by Peter Green) is one of the most famous guitars in blues-rock history.

tone.target: sustaining Marshall lead with delay and wah
tone.profile: sustaining Marshall lead with delay and wah
tone.summary: A high-gain, mid-focused signal chain using a UK 45 or UK 50 amp model, boosted by an OD pedal, shaped by wah, and finished with digital delay for classic lead tones.

rig.name: Gary Moore - Out In The Fields - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Tube Screamer boost for added sustain and mid-hump.
blocks.gap: The dedicated TS model is missing, but 'Boost' serves the function of a clean overdrive/boost pedal.

alternatives.reason: If more grit than pure boost is desired.

blocks.purpose: Provide decisive wah accents for lead playing.
Provide the necessary thick brit crunch and sustain before the amp.
blocks.gap: While a dedicated Plexi/Marshall model would be ideal, 'Distortion' provides the required high-gain foundation.

alternatives.reason: If a slightly dirtier, more aggressive tone is preferred.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/Plexi lead tone and bright upper mids.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound and definition.
Enhance the upper mids and cut unnecessary low-end mud.
Implement the required lead delay effect for sustain and space.
Add subtle natural ambience without muddying the lead tone.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the classic British lead tone.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage Marshall sound and upper-mid definition.
